Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaCorp International Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star one to ask a question and then record your name clearly when prompted. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaCorp International's Q2 2024 results. With me on the call are Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jonathan Hale.

Jonathan Hale:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. VitaCorp International delivered a solid Q2, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Rivera to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Rivera:
Thank you, Jonathan. As Jonathan mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $4.82 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year, or 4.8% on an organic basis—comprising 2.1% volume/mix growth, 1.7% pricing, and 1.0% from favorable FX in emerging markets. This topped our guidance midpoint and consensus expectations by 150 basis points, driven by share gains in key categories per recent IRI and Nielsen data. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.42, a robust 8.5% increase excluding one-time items like the $25 million tariff-related charge in North America. We generated $650 million in operating cash flow, up 12% year-over-year, enabling $400 million in share repurchases and a quarterly dividend hike to $0.48 per share, our 17th consecutive increase.

Diving deeper into P&L dynamics, gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 44.8%, fueled by full-year pricing actions totaling 7% across the portfolio—strategically front-loaded in H1 to offset 4-5% COGS inflation from cocoa, palm oil, and PET resin volatility—and productivity savings from our $150 million Enterprise Supply Chain Optimization program, or ESCO. This includes AI-driven demand sensing via our partnership with Blue Yonder, which improved forecast accuracy by 15% and reduced inventory by 8% year-over-year to $2.1 billion. Adjusted operating margin rose 140 basis points to 18.2%, with SG&A leverage from 2% lower A&P spend as a percentage of sales—redirected toward high-ROI digital and shopper marketing—offsetting $50 million in transitory labor and freight costs.

By segment, our Food & Beverage division, 58% of sales, grew organic sales 6.1% to $2.8 billion, led by VitaSnax protein-packed snacks, which captured 120 basis points of market share in the $25 billion U.S. better-for-you snack category. Volume/mix was 3.2%, bolstered by launches like our plant-based VitaBites line, now in 15,000 incremental ACV doors at Walmart and Kroger. Health & Beauty, 25% of sales, posted flat organic growth at $1.2 billion, with GlowEssence hyaluronic serums up 9% on e-commerce strength, now 22% of segment sales versus 18% last year, though offset by softer prestige volumes amid consumer trade-downs to mass-market. Household Essentials, 17% of sales, accelerated 7.4% organically to $820 million, driven by FreshGuard eco-friendly wipes, gaining traction in Europe with 200 basis points share per Kantar data.

Regionally, North America, 65% of sales, delivered 4.2% organic growth, resilient despite a 1% category ACV contraction; we outpaced the market by 300 basis points through targeted pricing in laundry and beverages. Europe, 20% of sales, grew 3.8% organically, navigating regulatory headwinds like the EU Green Deal packaging rules via our $100 million Circularity Fund, which recycled 25% more PET last quarter. Emerging Markets, 15% of sales including LatAm and Asia-Pac, were the star at 12.4% organic, powered by PureFlow expansions in Brazil and India—now a $500 million franchise—amid a favorable 8% regional CPG expansion per Euromonitor.

Before diving deeper into segment performance, let me unpack our organic sales growth, which came in at 5.2% for the quarter—right in line with our full-year guidance midpoint of 4-6%. This marks our third consecutive quarter of positive volume growth, a testament to the resilience of our portfolio amid a still-challenging macroeconomic backdrop. Organic sales growth excludes the impacts of FX, which headwinded us by 1.8% this quarter due to the strengthening USD, and M&A, which was negligible. Breaking it down into its core drivers—volume, price, and mix—we delivered volume growth of 2.1%, pricing of 2.5%, and favorable mix of 0.6%.

Starting with volume: 2.1% overall. This is our strongest volume quarter since Q4 2022, driven by share gains across 70% of our portfolio. In North America, 45% of sales, volume grew 3.2%, fueled by distribution expansion and everyday low pricing on core household staples. For instance, our Home Care division—like our flagship FreshGuard laundry cleaners—captured 110 basis points of market share in IRI-measured channels through targeted trade promotions and a 15% uplift in velocity from our CleanBoost concentrated pod innovation. This pod format, now in 85% ACV distribution up from 65% last year, resonated with eco-conscious millennials, aligning with Nielsen data showing a 12% category shift toward unit-dose formats.

In Europe, volume was flat at 0.1%, pressured by soft consumer sentiment in Germany and the UK, where private label penetration hit 28% per Kantar. However, we offset this with 4.5% growth in premium Beauty & Personal Care, led by GlowEssence serums, which gained 1.2 points of share in premium facial skincare—a segment growing at 7% annually per Euromonitor. Emerging Markets were the star, delivering 4.8% volume, with Latin America up 6.2% on robust demand for value-engineered snacks under our VitaSnax portfolio. In Asia-Pacific, Indonesia and India drove 5.1%, bolstered by rural distribution gains—we added 50,000 incremental outlets via Project VillageReach, our micro-depot initiative targeting 20% deeper penetration in tier-3 cities by FY2025.

Key enablers include our $450 million R&D investment in FY2023, yielding 22 new product launches, and a 10% increase in shopper marketing spend focused on high-velocity SKUs. We're also leveraging AI-driven forecasting via our DemandGenix platform, which improved in-stock rates to 96% from 92%, minimizing out-of-stocks during peak back-to-school and holiday prep seasons.

Moving to pricing: 2.5%. This reflects disciplined, data-led actions to recover input cost inflation, which cumulatively stands at 18% since FY2021 across commodities like palm oil, PET resin, and cocoa—the latter up 40% YTD per Bloomberg indices. We took list price increases averaging 4.2% early in the quarter, but elasticities remained favorable at -1.8 overall, better than the category average of -2.2x per our internal pricing analytics powered by advanced models.

In Q2, we executed targeted pricing actions across our portfolio, implementing an average list price increase of 5.2% globally, up from 4.1% in Q1. This was calibrated using our advanced pricing analytics platform—powered by AI-driven elasticity modeling in partnership with our data science team and tools like NielsenIQ and IRI data feeds. We focused on high-single-digit increases in categories with lower elasticity, such as our Health & Wellness segment—think PureFlow functional beverages and VitaSnax protein snacks—where we hiked prices by 7-9%, and more moderate 3-5% lifts in volume-driven staples like FreshGuard household cleaners.

The impact? These actions drove robust organic net revenue growth, with price/mix contributing significantly, more than offsetting any volume headwinds. Our net price realization came in strong after trade promotions, thanks to our optimized promotional calendar—we reduced ineffective trade spend by 12% year-over-year via zero-based budgeting and AI-forecasted lift models. Segment-wise, Food & Beverages saw 3.1% pricing, necessary to offset 22% cocoa inflation impacting our chocolate lines, while holding volume steady through smaller pouch packs. Beauty held pricing to 1.8%, prioritizing premiumization, which preserved volume in that unit. Regionally, Emerging Markets pricing was 3.8%, reflecting higher inflation pass-through tolerance, while North America was more modest at 2.0% to protect EDLP positioning against Walmart and Amazon's everyday pricing wars.

We've clawed back 85% of cumulative inflation to date, with gross margins expanding ahead of targets. North America saw 4.5% list price increases, focused on EDLP in club channels like Costco to defend against private label aggression. Elasticity was -1.2, mitigated by loyalty programs via our VitaRewards app, now with 15 million active users. In Europe, pricing averaged 6.1%, heaviest in Beauty, capitalizing on premiumization trends. Emerging markets leaned into 8.4% pricing, particularly in India and Brazil, where input costs remain elevated, paired with strong volumes.

Strategically, these actions align with our Value Above All framework. We've embedded machine learning into our pricing engine to simulate thousands of scenarios per category, incorporating forward curves for key inputs. This has improved forecast accuracy by 18%, allowing us to preempt competitive responses. Looking ahead, we'll maintain pricing discipline with 4-6% increases planned into Q4, emphasizing innovation-led pricing and expanding test-and-learn with retailers on hi-lo versus EDLP hybrids.

On the balance sheet, net debt stands at 2.3x EBITDA, down from 2.6x, with $1.8 billion in liquidity. ROIC improved to 14.2%, reflecting capital discipline—we idled two legacy plants and invested $200 million in high-velocity SKUs.

Now, turning to competitive activity and response, which remains a dynamic headwind across our portfolio. The CPG landscape continues to be shaped by persistent inflation, shifting consumer value perceptions, and aggressive moves from both branded peers and private label players. Branded competitors, particularly in beverages and snacks—like PepsiCo with their Gatorade Zero expansions and Mondelez's aggressive Oreo variety packs—ramped up everyday low pricing and BOGO promotions by an average of 12-15% year-over-year, per IRI and Nielsen multi-outlet scan data. This was most acute in North America, where trade spend as a percentage of revenue climbed to 22% industry-wide. Private labels from retailers like Walmart's Great Value and Amazon Basics intensified further, capturing 2.5 share points in household essentials.

The net impact on us? We saw a modest 1.2-point market share erosion in our North American Fabric Care segment—down to 27.8% ACV—primarily from P&G's Tide Pods refresh. However, this was more than offset in our Health & Wellness pillar, where we gained 1.8 points to 32.4% in plant-based nutrition. Regionally, in Europe, competitive pricing wars escalated with discounters like Lidl and Aldi, leading to a 0.8-point share dip for our Oral Care brands. Conversely, in Emerging Markets, we held firm, with flat-to-up share: +0.5 points in Brazil's beverage aisle.

Marketing and innovation fronts saw peers double down too. Colgate-Palmolive's global A&P surge behind Optic White pressured our whitening sub-segment, while Nestlé's veggie KitKats targeted our better-for-you confectionery. Our response has been multifaceted: innovation-led differentiation, like launching 14 SKUs this quarter—including a reformulated HydraGlow serum in Beauty driving 22% dollar sales velocity; supply chain resilience with 65% localized APAC production; and channel optimization, with e-commerce now 18% of sales.

We're not chasing share at any cost. Our focus is value over volume—targeting 2-3% organic growth through 300bps gross margin expansion via zero-based budgeting and procurement savings. Long-term, we're positioning for health megatrends: 60% of new launches tie to functional benefits.

Looking ahead to our outlook, for FY2024, we now guide organic sales growth of 4.0-5.0%, raised from 3.5-4.5%; adjusted EPS of $5.65-$5.85, up 7-10% at midpoint, including 53rd week benefit; and gross margin expansion of 150-200 bps. Q3 organic sales expected at 3.5-4.5%, with EPS of $1.35-$1.45. Key drivers: continued pricing discipline, another 3-4% planned; innovation pipeline with 15 new SKUs like low-sugar PureFlow Zero; and DTC/e-comm acceleration targeting 20% of total sales by year-end via Shopify integrations. Risks include FX volatility, we're 60% hedged, and potential U.S. recessionary pressures, but our 80/20 portfolio focus—80% of profits from top 20% SKUs—positions us defensively. We're accelerating sustainability initiatives, with 40% of packaging recyclable by Q4, on track for 2030 net-zero, unlocking premium shelf space at Target and Tesco. M&A remains opportunistic; post our acquisition of Indie Beauty Brands, we're eyeing bolt-ons in functional beverages.

In summary, VitaCorp is firing on all cylinders—delivering shareholder value while navigating CPG headwinds through innovation, efficiency, and consumer-centricity.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. We saw strong performance in our VitaSnax and PureFlow brands this quarter. As we dive into the drivers behind our record Q2 performance, marketing campaign effectiveness continues to be a cornerstone of our A&P strategy here at VitaCorp. In the CPG space, where we're battling incumbents like Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and Kraft Heinz for every share of wallet in categories like snacks, beverages, and household essentials, precision marketing is table stakes for sustainable growth. Our teams delivered exceptional results this quarter, with total marketing spend reaching $285 million, up 8% year-over-year, but generating a stellar 5.2x ROAS across the board, well ahead of our internal target of 4x and the industry benchmark of around 3.5x as reported by Nielsen and Kantar.

Overall campaign lift: Our integrated "Vita Refresh" summer activation—centered on our flagship PureFlow hydration drinks and new plant-based snack line—drove a 14% uplift in household penetration, per IRI data, contributing to $1.2 billion in incremental sales velocity. That's against a category backdrop where non-alcoholic beverages grew just 2.1% overall, per Circana, squeezed by inflation and private-label pressure. We saw market share gains of 120 basis points in energy drinks, taking us to 18.4% in North America.

By channel, digital continues to outperform. Our programmatic and social investments—$112 million, or 39% of spend—yielded a category-leading 7.1x ROAS, up from 6.2x last year. Key here was our heavy lift into retail media networks like Amazon DSP, Walmart Connect, and Target Roundel, which accounted for 28% of digital dollars. These gave us hyper-targeted access to high-intent shoppers; for instance, our PureFlow campaign on Amazon Ads generated a 22% conversion lift among Prime households purchasing competing products. Social media, via Meta and TikTok, was a powerhouse for awareness among Gen Z—our #VitaYourVitality challenge racked up 450 million impressions and a 3.5x engagement rate, translating to a 9% sales bump in e-comm channels per our proprietary attribution modeling.

Traditional media still plays, but we're optimizing ruthlessly. TV and CTV spend—$68 million—delivered 4.8x ROAS, bolstered by our shift to 65% CTV allocation. Streaming platforms like Hulu and Roku allowed for addressable TV buys tied to first-party data from our VitaRewards loyalty app, which now boasts 28 million active members, up 22% year-over-year. This zero-party data loop enabled 15-20% more efficient targeting. OOH and experiential rounded out at $45 million, with geo-fenced activations at music festivals driving 11% trial uplift.

Regionally, North America, our core market at 55% of revenue, hit 5.8x ROAS on the back of omnichannel synergy—think in-store sampling tied to Snapchat AR filters, lifting basket size by 18% in convenience channels. EMEA was softer at 4.2x due to HFSS advertising headwinds, but we pivoted to health-forward messaging for VitaSnax protein bars, gaining 80 bps share in the UK. APAC shone at 6.9x ROAS, fueled by e-comm dominance via Tmall and Shopee; our Lunar New Year campaign for VitaSnax achieved 25% year-over-year growth in premium segments. LATAM rounded out at 4.9x, with Brazil's soccer-themed promotions countering economic volatility.

Technically, we're ahead with AI-powered marketing mix modeling, incorporating clean-room data from Kroger and Instacart, reducing incrementality blind spots by 30%. We're rolling out dynamic creative optimization across 80% of digital campaigns, boosting CTR by 27% and shaving CAC from $4.20 to $3.65 per new household. Our "Vita Planet" ESG messaging resonated, lifting brand favorability 12 points to 74% per YouGov, and driving 16% premium price tolerance.

Strategically, these results underscore our precision at scale playbook: allocating 55% of A&P to performance channels versus 30% three years ago, while nurturing equity through purpose-driven storytelling. LTV from acquired customers is up 19% to $142. Looking forward, we'll invest another $1.2 billion in FY24 A&P, with 15% for emerging tech like shoppable CTV and metaverse pilots. Expect ROAS to expand to 5.5x by year-end, supporting our organic sales growth guidance amid cooling grocery inflation.

We're also excited about the launch of our new product, VitaBites plant-based snacks, which is already generating positive feedback and contributing to share gains in better-for-you categories.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Alex Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Alex Thompson:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

Lisa Chen:
Good morning, Alex. Absolutely. Our Vita Refresh campaign, as I detailed, centered on PureFlow and VitaSnax, delivering that 14% household penetration uplift and 5.2x ROAS overall. Specifically, the digital components on Amazon DSP and social drove 22% conversion lifts and 9% e-comm sales bumps, translating to over $1.2 billion in incremental velocity. It's resonating particularly with Gen Z through #VitaYourVitality, and we're seeing sustained basket size increases from omnichannel tie-ins. This has been key to our volume/mix gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Brian Patel with JPMorgan.

Brian Patel:
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Michael Rivera:
Thanks, Brian. Rising commodities like cocoa and palm oil remain a focus, up 40% YTD. Our pricing actions—5.2% average list increases—have clawed back 85% of cumulative inflation, with elasticities better than category averages. Combined with ESCO productivity savings and hedging—we're locking in palm oil forwards—and localized production at 65% in APAC, we're guiding 150-200 bps gross margin expansion. We'll continue 3-4% pricing discipline in H2 while monitoring supply chain stabilization post-Red Sea issues.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Chris Lee:
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Jonathan Hale:
Hi Chris. Inflation is pressuring wallets, but our premium lines like GlowEssence serums and VitaBites are holding resilient. Consumers are trading up in health and sustainability—premium now 32% of sales, up from 28%—driven by mix tailwinds of 0.6%. E-comm strength, now 22% in Health & Beauty, and ESG messaging via Vita Planet have lifted favorability and price tolerance by 16%. Our 80/20 focus keeps us defensive, outpacing categories by 300 bps in North America.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Dana Ruiz with Barclays.

Dana Ruiz:
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Dana. E-commerce was a bright spot, now 18-22% of sales depending on segment, up 5 points year-over-year. Digital ROAS hit 7.1x, with Amazon DSP and social driving 22% conversion lifts and 9% sales bumps. In Health & Beauty, it's 22% of sales, fueled by GlowEssence. Emerging markets shone via Tmall, adding 4 points share. We're targeting 20% total by year-end with Shopify DTC push and dynamic pricing pilots boosting online mix.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jonathan Hale for closing remarks.

Jonathan Hale:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the VitaCorp International Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
